questions.question_text: Which AWS feature automatically adjusts the number of EC2 instances in a group up or down based on demand, helping maintain application availability while controlling cost?
questions.explanation_correct: Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling automatically adds or removes EC2 instances according to conditions you define, such as CPU utilization, ensuring the right number of instances are running to handle the current load while avoiding the cost of over-provisioning.
questions.why_b_wrong: AWS Direct Connect provides a dedicated network connection between an on-premises location and AWS; it has no role in scaling compute capacity.
questions.why_c_wrong: Amazon Route 53 is a DNS and domain registration service; it routes traffic but doesn't scale the number of underlying compute instances.
questions.why_d_wrong: AWS CloudHSM provides dedicated hardware security modules for cryptographic operations, unrelated to instance scaling.

questions.question_text: A company wants business analysts to create interactive dashboards and visualizations from data stored across multiple AWS data sources, without writing code. Which AWS service is designed for this?
questions.explanation_correct: Amazon QuickSight is a business intelligence service that lets users create interactive dashboards and visualizations from various data sources with a point-and-click interface, designed for business analysts rather than requiring custom code.
questions.why_b_wrong: AWS Glue is a serverless data integration and ETL (extract, transform, load) service used to prepare and move data for analytics, not a dashboarding/visualization tool itself.
questions.why_c_wrong: Amazon Kinesis is used for ingesting and processing real-time streaming data, not for building interactive business dashboards.
questions.why_d_wrong: Amazon Redshift is a data warehouse service used to run fast analytical queries at scale; it's often a data source for QuickSight rather than the visualization layer itself.

questions.question_text: A company has a large volume of historical data (500 TB) stored on-premises that needs to be migrated into Amazon S3. The company's internet connection would take several months to transfer this volume of data. Which AWS service is designed for this use case?
questions.explanation_correct: AWS Snowball is a physical data transport device used to migrate large amounts of data into or out of AWS without relying on network bandwidth. For hundreds of terabytes that would take months over the internet, shipping a Snowball device is far faster and more cost-effective.
questions.why_a_wrong: Direct Connect provides a dedicated network link to AWS for ongoing, lower-latency connectivity — it still depends on network bandwidth, so it doesn't solve a one-time massive bulk transfer as efficiently as a physical device.
questions.why_c_wrong: CloudFront is a content delivery network for distributing content to end users; it has no role in migrating bulk data from on-premises to AWS.
questions.why_d_wrong: Storage Gateway connects on-premises environments to AWS storage for ongoing hybrid use, but for a single large one-time migration, Snowball is the purpose-built option.

questions.question_text: Which AWS service continuously tracks the configuration of AWS resources and evaluates whether they comply with a company's desired configuration rules, such as flagging an S3 bucket that becomes publicly accessible?
questions.explanation_correct: AWS Config records configuration changes to AWS resources over time and can evaluate them against rules you define, alerting you when a resource — such as an S3 bucket — drifts out of compliance, for example by becoming publicly accessible.
questions.why_b_wrong: Trusted Advisor provides general best-practice recommendations across cost, performance, security, and fault tolerance, but it isn't designed for continuous, rule-based configuration tracking over time.
questions.why_c_wrong: Secrets Manager stores and rotates credentials like database passwords and API keys; it has no role in tracking resource configuration compliance.
questions.why_d_wrong: License Manager tracks software license usage across an organization, unrelated to resource configuration compliance.

questions.question_text: A web application repeatedly queries the same product catalog data from its database for every page load, creating unnecessary load on the database. Which AWS service can reduce this load by storing frequently accessed data in memory for fast retrieval?
questions.explanation_correct: Amazon ElastiCache provides a fully managed in-memory caching layer (supporting Redis or Memcached) that stores frequently accessed data, reducing the number of direct queries hitting the primary database and improving application response times.
questions.why_b_wrong: AWS Database Migration Service (DMS) is used to migrate databases between environments or engines; it doesn't provide ongoing caching for live application traffic.
questions.why_c_wrong: Amazon Neptune is a managed graph database designed for highly connected data, such as social networks, not a caching layer.
questions.why_d_wrong: The AWS Schema Conversion Tool (SCT) helps convert database schemas when migrating between different database engines; it's unrelated to runtime caching.

questions.question_text: What is the relationship between an AWS Region and an Availability Zone (AZ)?
questions.explanation_correct: An AWS Region is a geographic area containing multiple, isolated Availability Zones. Each Availability Zone consists of one or more discrete data centers with independent power, cooling, and networking, designed so that a failure in one AZ doesn't affect others in the same Region.
questions.option_a: A Region is a single data center, and an AZ is a group of Regions
questions.option_b: An AZ is one or more discrete data centers within a Region, each with independent power, cooling, and networking
questions.option_c: Regions and AZs are the same thing, just different names
questions.option_d: An AZ spans multiple Regions across the world
questions.why_a_wrong: This reverses the relationship — a Region contains multiple AZs, not the other way around.
questions.why_c_wrong: Regions and AZs are distinct concepts at different levels of AWS's infrastructure hierarchy.
questions.why_d_wrong: An AZ is contained within a single Region; it does not span multiple Regions.

questions.question_text: A company is comparing its responsibilities when using Amazon RDS versus self-managing a database on Amazon EC2. Which statement accurately reflects how responsibility differs between the two?
questions.explanation_correct: Amazon RDS is a managed database service, so AWS handles much of the underlying operational work — OS patching, database engine patching, automated backups, and Multi-AZ failover — while the customer focuses on schema design, query optimization, and access control. Running a database on EC2 instead would require the customer to manage all of that themselves.
questions.option_a: With RDS, the customer must still patch the underlying database engine software and operating system
questions.option_b: With RDS, AWS manages tasks such as OS patching, database engine patching, and backups, reducing the customer's operational burden compared to running a database on EC2
questions.option_c: There is no difference in responsibility between RDS and a self-managed database on EC2
questions.option_d: With EC2, AWS automatically manages database backups for the customer
questions.why_a_wrong: This describes the EC2 self-managed scenario, not RDS — RDS specifically removes this burden from the customer.
questions.why_c_wrong: There is a significant difference: RDS is managed, while a self-installed database on EC2 places far more operational responsibility on the customer.
questions.why_d_wrong: On EC2, the customer — not AWS — is responsible for configuring and managing their own backup strategy for a self-installed database.

questions.question_text: A company transfers a large volume of data from an EC2 instance in one AWS Region to an EC2 instance in a different AWS Region. How is this data transfer typically billed compared to transferring data between two Availability Zones in the same Region?
questions.explanation_correct: Data transferred between AWS Regions typically incurs a per-GB charge, and this rate is generally higher than data transferred between Availability Zones within the same Region. Understanding this helps companies architect for cost efficiency when designing cross-Region workloads.
questions.option_a: Both transfers are always free of charge
questions.option_b: Inter-Region data transfer is generally charged, and is typically more expensive than transfer within the same Region
questions.option_c: Inter-Region transfer is always cheaper than intra-Region transfer
questions.option_d: Data transfer costs do not depend on whether the transfer crosses a Region boundary
questions.why_a_wrong: Some data transfer is free (such as inbound transfer or transfer within the same AZ in some cases), but inter-Region and many other transfer paths are not free.
questions.why_c_wrong: This reverses the typical cost relationship — inter-Region transfer is usually more expensive, not cheaper, than transfer within a Region.
questions.why_d_wrong: Data transfer pricing very much depends on the path the data takes — same AZ, cross-AZ, cross-Region, or out to the internet all have different rates.

questions.question_text: A data science team wants to build, train, and deploy machine learning models without having to manually set up and manage the underlying infrastructure for training or hosting. Which AWS service is purpose-built for this?
questions.explanation_correct: Amazon SageMaker AI is a fully managed service that provides every step of the machine learning workflow — from labeling and building, to training, tuning, and deploying models — without requiring the data science team to manage the underlying infrastructure themselves.
questions.why_b_wrong: Amazon Kendra is an intelligent enterprise search service that uses natural language processing to find answers within documents; it doesn't provide general-purpose ML model building and training.
questions.why_c_wrong: Amazon Polly converts text into lifelike speech; it's a purpose-built AI service, not a platform for building custom models.
questions.why_d_wrong: Amazon Comprehend performs natural language processing tasks like sentiment analysis and entity recognition on text; it's also a purpose-built service rather than a general model-building platform.

questions.question_text: A company currently purchases physical servers upfront and owns them outright. Moving to AWS, the company instead pays only for the compute it consumes each month. What change in cost structure does this represent?
questions.explanation_correct: Purchasing physical servers upfront is capital expenditure (CapEx) — a large investment made before any value is realized. Paying only for what's consumed each month is operating expenditure (OpEx) — ongoing costs tied to actual usage. Moving to this pay-as-you-go model is a shift from CapEx to OpEx.
questions.option_a: A shift from variable cost to fixed cost
questions.option_b: A shift from operating expenditure to capital expenditure
questions.option_c: A shift from capital expenditure to operating expenditure
questions.why_a_wrong: This describes the opposite direction of the actual shift described in the scenario.
questions.why_b_wrong: This also describes the opposite direction — the company is moving away from capital expenditure, not toward it.
questions.why_d_wrong: The cost structure does change significantly: from a large upfront investment to a flexible, consumption-based ongoing expense.

questions.question_text: What is the key difference between an IAM user and an IAM role?
questions.explanation_correct: An IAM user represents a person or application and typically has long-term credentials, such as a password or access keys. An IAM role, by contrast, is assumed temporarily — by a user, application, or AWS service — and provides temporary security credentials, which is more secure for many use cases.
questions.option_a: An IAM user has long-term credentials associated with a specific person or application, while an IAM role is assumed temporarily and does not have long-term credentials
questions.option_b: An IAM role can only be used by the AWS root user
questions.option_c: An IAM user can only access Amazon S3, while an IAM role can access all AWS services
questions.option_d: There is no difference; the terms are interchangeable
questions.why_b_wrong: IAM roles can be assumed by IAM users, applications, AWS services, or federated identities — not just the root user.
questions.why_c_wrong: Access permissions for both IAM users and roles are defined by attached policies; neither is inherently limited to S3 or unlimited to all services by default.
questions.why_d_wrong: IAM users and roles are distinct concepts with different credential models and use cases.

questions.question_text: How does the shared responsibility model shift when a company moves from using Amazon EC2 to using AWS Lambda?
questions.explanation_correct: As services become more abstracted and managed, AWS takes on more of the operational burden. With Lambda, AWS manages the servers, operating system, and runtime environment, so the customer is responsible only for their application code and configuring appropriate permissions — a smaller share of responsibility compared to EC2.
questions.option_a: The customer takes on more responsibility, since Lambda requires manual patching of servers
questions.option_b: AWS takes on more responsibility, since Lambda is a fully managed, serverless service where AWS manages the underlying compute infrastructure and runtime
questions.option_c: There is no difference in shared responsibility between EC2 and Lambda
questions.option_d: The customer becomes responsible for the physical hardware running Lambda functions
questions.why_a_wrong: This is backwards — Lambda actually reduces the customer's operational responsibility compared to EC2, since there's no OS to patch.
questions.why_c_wrong: There is a meaningful difference: EC2 requires the customer to manage the OS, while Lambda does not.
questions.why_d_wrong: Customers never manage physical hardware under any AWS service, including Lambda.

questions.question_text: Why is it true that Availability Zones within the same AWS Region do not share a single point of failure?
questions.explanation_correct: Each Availability Zone consists of one or more discrete data centers with their own independent power, cooling, and physical location, even though they are connected with high-bandwidth, low-latency networking. This physical separation is exactly why a failure affecting one AZ — such as a power outage — does not affect the others.
questions.option_a: Because each Availability Zone has independent power, cooling, and physical location from the others
questions.option_b: Because all Availability Zones in a Region use the exact same physical building
questions.option_c: Because Availability Zones are virtual and don't have physical infrastructure
questions.option_d: Because only one Availability Zone is active at a time
questions.why_b_wrong: AZs are physically distinct facilities, not the same building, which is precisely what allows them to fail independently.
questions.why_c_wrong: AZs are very much physical — real data centers with real hardware — not purely virtual constructs.
questions.why_d_wrong: Multiple AZs within a Region typically run concurrently; workloads can be actively distributed across them rather than only one being active.

questions.question_text: A company wants to define its AWS infrastructure — including VPCs, subnets, and EC2 instances — in a text template so that environments can be created consistently and repeatedly without manual console clicks. Which approach does this describe?
questions.explanation_correct: Infrastructure as Code (IaC) means defining infrastructure in a machine-readable template so it can be created, updated, and replicated consistently. AWS CloudFormation is the AWS-native service for this, letting you describe resources like VPCs and EC2 instances in JSON or YAML templates.
questions.option_a: Infrastructure as Code (IaC) using AWS CloudFormation
questions.option_b: Manually provisioning resources through the AWS Management Console each time
questions.option_c: Using AWS Snowball to physically ship infrastructure
questions.option_d: Using Amazon CloudFront to deploy infrastructure
questions.why_b_wrong: Manually clicking through the console is the opposite of IaC — it's error-prone, slow, and difficult to repeat exactly each time.
questions.why_c_wrong: AWS Snowball is a physical data transport device for bulk data migration, unrelated to defining infrastructure as code.
questions.why_d_wrong: Amazon CloudFront is a content delivery network, not an infrastructure provisioning or templating tool.

questions.question_text: Under the AWS shared responsibility model, which of the following is the customer's responsibility when running an application on Amazon EC2?
questions.explanation_correct: For EC2 (an unmanaged, infrastructure-level service), AWS is responsible for the hardware, virtualization layer, and facilities — but the customer is responsible for the guest operating system, including patching, application software, and network/firewall configuration.
questions.option_a: Maintaining the physical hardware that hosts EC2 instances
questions.option_b: Patching the guest operating system running on the EC2 instance
questions.option_c: Ensuring power and cooling to the data center
questions.why_a_wrong: Maintaining physical hardware is part of 'security of the cloud,' which is entirely AWS's responsibility.
questions.why_c_wrong: Power and cooling to the data center are part of the physical infrastructure AWS manages, not something the customer ever touches.
questions.why_d_wrong: Replacing physical disks is hardware maintenance performed by AWS at the facility level.

questions.question_text: A company wants to protect data so that it cannot be read by anyone who intercepts it while it travels between a client application and an AWS service over the internet. Which concept addresses this requirement?
questions.explanation_correct: Encryption in transit protects data while it moves across a network, typically using protocols like TLS/SSL, such as those provided by AWS Certificate Manager. This prevents data from being read if intercepted during transmission.
questions.why_a_wrong: Encryption at rest protects stored data on disk, such as in S3 or EBS, but doesn't address data while it's actively moving across a network.
questions.why_c_wrong: Data residency refers to the geographic location where data is stored to meet legal or regulatory requirements, not protection during transmission.
questions.why_d_wrong: Data classification is the process of categorizing data by sensitivity level; it's a precursor to deciding what protections to apply, not the protection itself.

questions.question_text: A media company has a large library of video files that are accessed frequently for the first 30 days after upload, then rarely accessed afterward. Which TWO Amazon S3 features help reduce long-term storage costs for this access pattern? (Select TWO)
questions.explanation_correct: S3 Lifecycle policies (A) let you define rules to automatically move objects to cheaper storage classes, such as S3 Standard-IA or Glacier, after a set number of days. S3 Intelligent-Tiering (B) goes a step further by automatically monitoring access patterns and moving objects between tiers without you having to predict exact timing — both directly reduce costs for data whose access frequency drops over time.
questions.option_a: S3 Lifecycle policies, which automatically transition objects to lower-cost storage classes after a defined period
questions.option_b: S3 Intelligent-Tiering, which automatically moves objects between access tiers based on changing access patterns
questions.option_c: S3 Transfer Acceleration, which speeds up uploads over long distances
questions.option_d: S3 Cross-Region Replication, which copies objects to a bucket in another Region
questions.option_e: S3 Object Lock, which prevents objects from being deleted for a retention period
questions.why_c_wrong: Transfer Acceleration speeds up data going into S3 over long distances; it has no effect on storage costs for data already stored.
questions.why_d_wrong: Cross-Region Replication is for resiliency and latency purposes — it actually adds storage cost by maintaining a second copy, rather than reducing it.
questions.why_e_wrong: Object Lock is a compliance and data-protection feature that prevents deletion; it doesn't change storage class or reduce cost.

questions.question_text: A data-processing job runs intensive numerical simulations and benefits from instances with the highest possible vCPU performance per dollar, with less concern for memory size. Which EC2 instance family category is best suited for this job?
questions.explanation_correct: Compute optimized instance families are designed for compute-bound workloads that benefit from high-performance processors, such as batch processing, scientific modeling, and high-performance computing — exactly the profile of a CPU-intensive simulation job.
questions.why_a_wrong: Memory optimized instances are designed for workloads that process large datasets in memory, such as in-memory databases — not primarily CPU-bound simulations.
questions.why_c_wrong: Storage optimized instances are designed for workloads requiring high, sequential read/write access to large datasets on local storage, not raw compute performance.
questions.why_d_wrong: General purpose instances provide a balance of compute, memory, and networking, suitable for a broad range of workloads, but they aren't optimized specifically for maximum compute performance.

questions.question_text: Which of the following tasks can ONLY be performed by the AWS account root user, and not delegated to an IAM user, even one with full administrator permissions?
questions.explanation_correct: Closing an AWS account is one of a small number of highly sensitive tasks that can only be performed by the root user, regardless of how much permission an IAM user is granted. Other root-only tasks include changing the account's root email address and viewing certain billing/tax information.
questions.option_b: Changing the AWS support plan for the account
questions.why_a_wrong: Launching an EC2 instance is a routine task that any IAM user with appropriate permissions can perform.
questions.why_b_wrong: Changing the support plan can typically be delegated to an IAM user with the right billing permissions; it is not restricted to root only.
questions.why_d_wrong: Creating an S3 bucket is a standard task achievable by any IAM user with sufficient S3 permissions.

questions.question_text: A company wants to make a deliberate choice about how its sensitive customer data is encrypted before storing it in Amazon S3. Under the shared responsibility model, whose responsibility is this decision?
questions.explanation_correct: Customers are responsible for deciding how to classify their data and which encryption options to apply, such as choosing server-side encryption with AWS KMS keys or encrypting data themselves before upload. AWS provides the tools and capability, but the decision and configuration of data protection is on the customer.
questions.why_a_wrong: AWS provides encryption capabilities and secures the underlying infrastructure, but does not make data classification or encryption decisions on the customer's behalf.
questions.why_c_wrong: The shared responsibility model isn't a fixed 50/50 split — responsibilities are divided by category, not by percentage, and this particular decision falls to the customer.
questions.why_d_wrong: AWS Support provides technical assistance but does not make data protection decisions for a customer's workload.

questions.question_text: A company wants to protect its public-facing web application from common web exploits such as SQL injection and cross-site scripting (XSS). Which AWS service is designed for this purpose?
questions.explanation_correct: AWS WAF (Web Application Firewall) lets you create rules that filter and monitor HTTP/HTTPS requests, blocking common web exploits like SQL injection and XSS before they reach your application.
questions.why_a_wrong: AWS Shield protects against Distributed Denial of Service (DDoS) attacks at the network and transport layer, which is a different threat category from application-layer exploits like SQL injection.
questions.why_c_wrong: Amazon Inspector scans EC2 instances and container images for software vulnerabilities; it doesn't filter live web traffic for exploit patterns in real time.
questions.why_d_wrong: AWS KMS manages cryptographic keys for encryption; it has no role in filtering malicious web requests.

questions.question_text: A company is evaluating its EC2 fleet and notices that several instances are consistently using only 10% of their provisioned CPU and memory. What cost-optimization practice should the company apply?
questions.explanation_correct: Rightsizing means matching instance types and sizes to actual workload requirements. If instances are consistently underutilized, downsizing them to a smaller, cheaper instance type reduces cost without affecting performance.
questions.why_b_wrong: Sharding is a database scaling technique that splits data across multiple smaller databases; it isn't related to matching compute size to utilization.
questions.why_c_wrong: Vertical partitioning is a database design concept, not a cost-optimization technique for compute sizing.
questions.why_d_wrong: Cross-region replication duplicates data across AWS Regions for durability or latency reasons; it doesn't address underutilized compute capacity.

questions.question_text: A company needs to continuously collect evidence to demonstrate that its AWS environment meets a specific compliance framework, such as PCI DSS, ahead of an upcoming audit. Which AWS service is purpose-built for this?
questions.explanation_correct: AWS Audit Manager continuously collects evidence from your AWS environment against industry standards and regulations, helping you assess risk and prepare for audits without manually gathering evidence yourself.
questions.why_b_wrong: AWS Shield protects against DDoS attacks; it has no role in evidence collection for compliance audits.
questions.why_c_wrong: Amazon Macie discovers and classifies sensitive data in S3, which can support data-governance efforts, but it is not designed to map evidence to broad compliance frameworks like Audit Manager does.
questions.why_d_wrong: AWS Firewall Manager centrally manages firewall rules like WAF and Shield Advanced across accounts; it doesn't generate compliance evidence.

questions.question_text: A healthcare company must keep patient data within a specific country to comply with local data residency laws, while also serving users in a different country with low latency. Which AWS global infrastructure feature addresses both needs?
questions.explanation_correct: AWS Regions are located in many countries around the world. By choosing which Region to deploy specific workloads in, a company can keep regulated data within the required country while also placing other workloads in Regions closer to additional user bases for lower latency.
questions.option_a: Using a single Availability Zone for all workloads
questions.option_b: Deploying workloads into multiple AWS Regions, choosing the Region location based on data residency and proximity to users
questions.option_d: Using only edge locations with no Regions at all
questions.why_a_wrong: A single AZ doesn't address data residency requirements across multiple countries or improve latency for users elsewhere.
questions.why_c_wrong: Disabling encryption does not address data residency requirements and would actually weaken the company's compliance posture.
questions.why_d_wrong: Edge locations cache content for low latency but don't provide the durable, compliant data storage and processing that Regions do.

questions.question_text: Which AWS service is a scalable Domain Name System (DNS) web service that also supports domain registration and health checking for routing traffic?
questions.explanation_correct: Amazon Route 53 is AWS's DNS service, translating domain names into IP addresses, and it also supports domain registration and health checks that can be used to route traffic away from unhealthy endpoints.
questions.why_b_wrong: AWS Global Accelerator improves availability and performance for global applications by routing traffic through the AWS global network, but it isn't a DNS or domain registration service.
questions.why_c_wrong: Amazon API Gateway is used to create, publish, and manage APIs; it doesn't provide DNS resolution or domain registration.
questions.why_d_wrong: AWS PrivateLink provides private connectivity between VPCs and services without traversing the public internet; it has no domain registration or DNS function.

questions.question_text: A company wants access to a dedicated Technical Account Manager (TAM) who provides proactive guidance and operational reviews for its AWS environment. Which AWS Support plan includes this?
questions.explanation_correct: AWS Enterprise Support is the plan that includes a dedicated Technical Account Manager (TAM), who provides proactive guidance, operational reviews, and works with the customer to optimize performance, plan for events, and resolve issues — a level of dedicated support not included in the other tiers.
questions.why_a_wrong: Basic Support is free and includes only access to AWS documentation, forums, and a limited set of checks — no TAM and no proactive guidance.
questions.why_b_wrong: Developer Support provides general guidance via email/chat during business hours, but it does not include a dedicated TAM.
questions.why_c_wrong: Business Support provides 24/7 access to Cloud Support Engineers and full Trusted Advisor checks, but it still does not include a dedicated TAM — that begins specifically at the Enterprise tiers.

questions.question_text: Which AWS service uses machine learning to continuously analyze account and network activity in order to detect threats such as compromised EC2 instances or unusual API calls indicating unauthorized access?
questions.explanation_correct: Amazon GuardDuty is a threat detection service that uses machine learning, anomaly detection, and threat intelligence feeds to continuously monitor for malicious or unauthorized activity, such as a compromised instance communicating with a known malicious IP address.
questions.why_b_wrong: AWS Resource Access Manager (RAM) allows sharing AWS resources across accounts; it has no threat-detection capability.
questions.why_c_wrong: AWS Organizations manages multiple AWS accounts centrally, including consolidated billing and policy enforcement, but doesn't perform threat detection itself.
questions.why_d_wrong: The AWS Health Dashboard reports on the operational status of AWS services and any account-specific events, not security threats.

questions.question_text: Which AWS service records a history of API calls made within an AWS account, including who made the call, when, and from which IP address, for security analysis and auditing?
questions.explanation_correct: AWS CloudTrail logs API activity across an AWS account, capturing details such as the identity of the caller, the time of the call, the source IP address, and the request parameters. This log is essential for security auditing and incident investigation.
questions.why_a_wrong: CloudWatch monitors metrics, logs application and infrastructure performance, and triggers alarms — it's about operational monitoring, not detailed API call history.
questions.why_c_wrong: Audit Manager helps continuously collect evidence to assess whether controls meet compliance frameworks; it consumes data like CloudTrail logs rather than capturing the raw API calls itself.
questions.why_d_wrong: GuardDuty analyzes account activity (including CloudTrail logs) to detect threats, but it doesn't itself record the raw history of API calls.

questions.question_text: Which AWS service decouples application components by allowing them to send, store, and receive messages between software components at any volume, helping prevent message loss if a downstream component is temporarily unavailable?
questions.explanation_correct: Amazon SQS (Simple Queue Service) is a fully managed message queuing service that decouples application components, holding messages reliably until the receiving component is ready to process them, even if that component is temporarily down.
questions.why_b_wrong: Amazon Connect is a cloud-based contact center service used for managing customer service interactions, unrelated to decoupling application messaging.
questions.why_c_wrong: AWS Amplify helps developers build and deploy full-stack web and mobile applications; it doesn't provide message queuing between components.
questions.why_d_wrong: Amazon WorkSpaces provides managed virtual desktops for end users, unrelated to application messaging architecture.

questions.question_text: According to the AWS Well-Architected Framework, which pillar is primarily concerned with the ability to detect failures, recover quickly, and dynamically acquire resources to meet demand?
questions.explanation_correct: The Reliability pillar focuses on a workload's ability to perform its intended function correctly and consistently, including recovering from failures, dynamically acquiring resources to meet demand, and mitigating disruptions.
questions.why_a_wrong: Cost Optimization focuses on avoiding unnecessary costs and understanding spending over time, not on failure recovery.
questions.why_c_wrong: Operational Excellence focuses on running and monitoring systems to deliver business value and continuously improving processes, but the specific focus on failure recovery and dynamic scaling belongs to Reliability.
questions.why_d_wrong: Sustainability focuses on minimizing the environmental impact of running cloud workloads, such as energy and resource efficiency.

questions.question_text: Which TWO EC2 purchasing options provide a discount compared to On-Demand pricing in exchange for a usage or term commitment? (Select TWO)
questions.explanation_correct: Reserved Instances (A) provide a significant discount in exchange for committing to a 1- or 3-year term for a specific instance configuration. Savings Plans (B) provide a similar discount but more flexibly, based on committing to a consistent dollar amount of usage per hour rather than a specific instance type. Both trade commitment for savings.
questions.option_d: Spot Instances priced at the full On-Demand rate
questions.option_e: Dedicated Hosts used only for compliance, with no term commitment
questions.why_c_wrong: On-Demand Instances are the baseline, full-price, no-commitment option — they don't offer a discount for commitment, since there isn't one.
questions.why_d_wrong: Spot Instances do offer steep discounts, but specifically by bidding on spare capacity, not through a term commitment — and pricing them 'at the full On-Demand rate' contradicts what Spot pricing actually is.
questions.why_e_wrong: Dedicated Hosts can be purchased On-Demand or reserved; used purely for compliance with no term commitment, this option as described doesn't provide a commitment-based discount.

questions.question_text: Which AWS service allows customers to access AWS compliance reports, such as SOC and PCI DSS reports, to support their own audit and regulatory requirements?
questions.explanation_correct: AWS Artifact is the central resource for compliance-related documentation, including SOC reports, PCI DSS reports, and agreements such as the Business Associate Addendum (BAA). Customers use it on-demand to support their own audits and compliance programs.
questions.why_a_wrong: AWS Config tracks and evaluates the configuration of AWS resources over time, but does not provide AWS's own compliance attestation documents.
questions.why_c_wrong: AWS CloudTrail logs API activity within an AWS account for auditing customer actions, not for accessing AWS's compliance certifications.
questions.why_d_wrong: Amazon Inspector scans workloads for software vulnerabilities and unintended network exposure; it doesn't provide compliance reports about AWS itself.

questions.question_text: A company needs a dedicated, private network connection between its on-premises data center and AWS that does not traverse the public internet, in order to achieve consistent network performance for a large, steady volume of data. Which AWS service is designed for this?
questions.explanation_correct: AWS Direct Connect establishes a dedicated, private network connection from an on-premises location to AWS, bypassing the public internet entirely. This provides more consistent network performance and is well-suited for large, steady data transfer needs compared to internet-based connections.
questions.why_b_wrong: AWS Site-to-Site VPN creates an encrypted connection over the public internet, which is more flexible to set up but doesn't offer the same consistent, dedicated bandwidth as a physical Direct Connect link.
questions.why_c_wrong: Amazon CloudFront is a content delivery network for distributing content to end users globally; it isn't designed for dedicated on-premises-to-AWS connectivity.
questions.why_d_wrong: AWS Transit Gateway simplifies connecting multiple VPCs and on-premises networks through a central hub, but the dedicated, non-internet physical link itself is provided by Direct Connect.

questions.question_text: A software vendor already owns perpetual licenses for a database engine and wants to continue using those licenses when running the database on Amazon EC2, instead of paying for new licenses included with a managed AWS service. Which licensing approach does this describe?
questions.explanation_correct: Bring Your Own License (BYOL) lets a company use software licenses it already owns on AWS infrastructure, rather than paying for licensing bundled into a managed service. This is common for commercial database engines where a company has existing license agreements.
questions.why_b_wrong: The included license model is the opposite scenario — AWS bundles the license cost into the service price, such as with some Amazon RDS license-included options.
questions.why_c_wrong: Reserved Instance pricing is a compute purchasing option based on commitment term, unrelated to software licensing strategy.
questions.why_d_wrong: Consolidated billing combines billing across multiple AWS accounts in an organization; it has nothing to do with software licensing models.

questions.question_text: A retail company currently runs a fixed number of on-premises servers sized for its busiest shopping day. During the rest of the year, most of that capacity sits unused. Which AWS Cloud benefit directly addresses this problem?
questions.explanation_correct: Elasticity is the ability to automatically scale compute, storage, and other resources up or down based on demand, and only pay for what is used. This removes the need to size infrastructure for peak load year-round, which is exactly the problem described: idle capacity for most of the year just to handle one busy day.
questions.why_b_wrong: Global reach refers to AWS's worldwide footprint of Regions and edge locations, which helps reduce latency for distributed users — it doesn't address matching capacity to fluctuating demand.
questions.why_c_wrong: High availability is about minimizing downtime through redundant components and failover, not about scaling resources to match variable demand.
questions.why_d_wrong: Fault tolerance means a system continues operating even if a component fails. It's related to resilience, not to the cost and capacity-matching problem in this scenario.

questions.question_text: Which AWS tool allows a company to visualize, understand, and analyze its AWS costs and usage over time, including filtering by service, account, or tag?
questions.explanation_correct: AWS Cost Explorer provides an interface to visualize, understand, and analyze AWS costs and usage patterns over time, with the ability to filter and group data by dimensions such as service, linked account, or cost allocation tag.
questions.why_b_wrong: Trusted Advisor provides best-practice recommendations across categories like cost, performance, and security, but it isn't built for the detailed historical cost visualization that Cost Explorer offers.
questions.why_c_wrong: The AWS Health Dashboard reports on the operational status of AWS services, not cost analysis.
questions.why_d_wrong: AWS Organizations manages multiple accounts and consolidated billing structurally, but the actual cost visualization and analysis is done through Cost Explorer.

questions.question_text: A company wants its employees to sign in to AWS using their existing corporate Active Directory credentials, without creating separate IAM users for each employee. Which AWS service supports this centrally?
questions.explanation_correct: AWS IAM Identity Center (successor to AWS Single Sign-On) enables centralized federated access, allowing employees to sign in using an existing identity provider — such as corporate Active Directory — and access multiple AWS accounts without needing individual IAM users in each one.
questions.why_b_wrong: Amazon Cognito provides authentication and user management for customer-facing applications, such as a mobile app's sign-up and sign-in flow, rather than centralized workforce access to AWS accounts.
questions.why_c_wrong: AWS KMS manages encryption keys; it has no role in user authentication or federated sign-in.
questions.why_d_wrong: AWS Secrets Manager stores and rotates sensitive credentials like database passwords; it doesn't manage employee identity federation.

questions.question_text: A company needs a database for an e-commerce application with structured order, customer, and inventory data that requires complex joins and transactions across multiple tables. Which type of database is most appropriate?
questions.explanation_correct: Relational databases like Amazon RDS are designed for structured data with defined relationships between tables, supporting complex joins, transactions, and strong consistency — exactly what's needed for orders, customers, and inventory data that relate to one another.
questions.option_a: A relational database such as Amazon RDS
questions.option_b: A key-value NoSQL database such as Amazon DynamoDB
questions.option_c: An in-memory cache such as Amazon ElastiCache
questions.option_d: An object storage service such as Amazon S3
questions.why_b_wrong: DynamoDB is a NoSQL key-value/document database, well suited for simple lookups at massive scale, but less suited to complex multi-table joins than a relational database.
questions.why_c_wrong: ElastiCache is an in-memory caching layer used to speed up access to frequently requested data; it's not designed to be a system of record for transactional order data.
questions.why_d_wrong: Amazon S3 stores unstructured objects like files and images; it doesn't support structured queries, joins, or transactions needed for relational e-commerce data.

questions.question_text: Which security practice grants users only the permissions they need to perform their job, and nothing more?
questions.explanation_correct: The principle of least privilege means granting only the minimum set of permissions required to perform a task. This limits the potential damage if credentials are compromised or misused.
questions.why_b_wrong: Defense in depth refers to layering multiple security controls so that if one fails, others still provide protection — a broader strategy, not specifically about minimal permission scope.
questions.why_c_wrong: Separation of duties divides critical tasks among multiple people so that no single person can complete a sensitive action alone; it's related but distinct from least privilege.
questions.why_d_wrong: Federated identity allows users to authenticate using an external identity provider; it's about authentication source, not the scope of permissions granted.

questions.question_text: Which AWS storage service provides a fully managed, scalable file system that can be mounted concurrently by multiple Linux-based EC2 instances using the NFS protocol?
questions.explanation_correct: Amazon EFS provides a fully managed, elastic NFS file system that can be mounted concurrently by many EC2 instances at the same time, making it ideal for shared file access across a fleet of Linux servers.
questions.why_b_wrong: Amazon EBS volumes are block storage typically attached to only one EC2 instance at a time (with some exceptions for Multi-Attach), not a general-purpose shared file system across many instances.
questions.why_c_wrong: S3 Glacier is a low-cost archival object storage class, not a file system that can be mounted by EC2 instances.
questions.why_d_wrong: AWS Storage Gateway connects on-premises applications to AWS storage for hybrid use cases; it isn't itself a directly mountable shared file system for EC2.

questions.question_text: Which cloud economics concept describes the cost advantage AWS can offer customers because it aggregates the usage of hundreds of thousands of customers, achieving higher levels of efficiency than any single company could on its own?
questions.explanation_correct: Economies of scale means that as AWS's infrastructure grows and serves more customers in aggregate, the cost per unit of compute, storage, or networking decreases. AWS passes these savings on to customers through continual price reductions.
questions.why_a_wrong: Rightsizing is about matching individual resource sizes to workload needs, not about AWS's aggregate purchasing power.
questions.why_c_wrong: Total cost of ownership (TCO) is a broader calculation comparing all costs of running infrastructure on-premises versus in the cloud, not specifically about AWS's scale advantage.
questions.why_d_wrong: Capacity reservation is an EC2 feature that reserves compute capacity in a specific AZ; it's unrelated to economies of scale.

questions.question_text: A company wants to purchase a third-party intrusion detection or security monitoring solution that is already pre-configured to work within AWS. Where should the company look for these offerings?
questions.explanation_correct: AWS Marketplace is a digital catalog where customers can find, buy, and deploy third-party software, including security products like intrusion detection systems, firewalls, and monitoring tools, that are pre-configured to run on AWS.
questions.why_b_wrong: S3 Glacier is a low-cost archival storage class for infrequently accessed data; it has no relation to discovering software products.
questions.why_c_wrong: The AWS Snow Family is a set of physical devices for offline data transfer and edge computing, unrelated to software procurement.
questions.why_d_wrong: Amazon Route 53 is a DNS and domain registration service, unrelated to finding third-party security software.

questions.question_text: Which component of an Amazon VPC is used to control inbound and outbound traffic at the subnet level, evaluating rules in numbered order for both allow and deny rules?
questions.explanation_correct: A Network Access Control List (Network ACL) operates at the subnet level and evaluates numbered rules in order, supporting both allow and deny rules. This is different from security groups, which operate at the instance level and only support allow rules.
questions.why_a_wrong: Security groups operate at the instance (elastic network interface) level and only support allow rules, not numbered allow/deny rules at the subnet level.
questions.why_c_wrong: An internet gateway allows communication between a VPC and the internet; it doesn't itself filter traffic with numbered rules.
questions.why_d_wrong: A NAT gateway allows instances in a private subnet to initiate outbound traffic to the internet without being directly reachable from it; it isn't a traffic-filtering rule set.

questions.question_text: A company keeps some sensitive workloads in its own on-premises data center for regulatory reasons but runs other workloads on AWS, with both environments connected and integrated. What is this deployment model called?
questions.explanation_correct: A hybrid cloud deployment combines on-premises infrastructure with AWS Cloud resources, integrated so that workloads, data, and applications can interact across both environments. This is common for regulatory, latency, or legacy-system reasons.
questions.why_a_wrong: Public cloud refers to running entirely within a shared cloud provider's infrastructure, with no on-premises component.
questions.why_c_wrong: Private cloud refers to cloud-like infrastructure dedicated to a single organization, typically run on-premises, without using a public provider like AWS.
questions.why_d_wrong: Multi-cloud refers to using multiple distinct public cloud providers (such as AWS and another vendor) together, not a combination of on-premises and one cloud provider.

questions.question_text: A company experiences a sudden, massive spike in traffic that appears designed to overwhelm its public-facing application and make it unavailable to legitimate users. Which AWS service is specifically designed to protect against this type of attack?
questions.explanation_correct: AWS Shield provides protection against Distributed Denial of Service (DDoS) attacks. AWS Shield Standard is automatically enabled at no extra cost for all customers, while Shield Advanced provides additional protections and 24/7 access to the AWS DDoS Response Team for an additional fee.
questions.why_b_wrong: Amazon Macie discovers and classifies sensitive data within S3; it has no role in mitigating denial-of-service traffic.
questions.why_c_wrong: AWS Directory Service provides managed directory services for identity management, unrelated to DDoS mitigation.
questions.why_d_wrong: AWS CloudHSM provides dedicated hardware security modules for cryptographic key storage, not traffic-based attack protection.

questions.question_text: A company has variable compute needs across several EC2 instance families and Regions, and wants a flexible pricing commitment that automatically applies a discount to whichever compute usage it incurs, rather than locking into a specific instance type. Which AWS pricing model fits this requirement?
questions.explanation_correct: Savings Plans offer a flexible pricing model where a company commits to a consistent amount of compute usage (measured in $/hour) for a 1- or 3-year term, and the discount automatically applies across eligible instance families, sizes, and Regions — more flexible than a traditional Reserved Instance tied to a specific configuration.
questions.why_b_wrong: Spot Instances are unrelated to commitment-based discounts; they offer steep discounts on spare capacity but with the risk of interruption.
questions.why_c_wrong: Dedicated Instances run on hardware dedicated to a single customer for compliance reasons, not a flexible usage-based discount commitment.
questions.why_d_wrong: Capacity Reservations reserve EC2 capacity in a specific Availability Zone for a specific instance type, ensuring availability — but they don't provide the flexible cross-family pricing discount that Savings Plans offer.

questions.question_text: A company wants to reduce the manual effort its operations team spends provisioning and configuring new environments for each project. Which cloud economics benefit does automation primarily provide in this case?
questions.explanation_correct: Automating provisioning and configuration tasks — for example using AWS CloudFormation or Systems Manager — reduces the time staff spend on repetitive manual work, lowering operational costs and reducing the risk of human error.
questions.option_b: Reduced operational costs through fewer manual tasks
questions.option_d: Improved physical security of data centers
questions.why_a_wrong: Data transfer costs are determined by the volume of data moving between Regions, AZs, or out to the internet; automation of provisioning doesn't directly change this.
questions.why_c_wrong: Automation typically reduces operating costs rather than increasing capital expenditure; in fact, cloud usage in general shifts spend away from CapEx.
questions.why_d_wrong: Physical security of data centers is entirely AWS's responsibility regardless of whether a customer automates their own provisioning tasks.

questions.question_text: Which type of EC2 storage is physically attached to the host computer, offers very high I/O performance, but loses all its data when the instance is stopped or terminated?
questions.explanation_correct: Instance store volumes are physically attached to the host hardware running an EC2 instance, providing very high, low-latency I/O performance. However, the data is ephemeral — it's lost if the instance is stopped, terminated, or the underlying hardware fails.
questions.why_a_wrong: Amazon EBS volumes are network-attached, persistent block storage that survives instance stop/start (though not necessarily termination unless configured to persist), unlike instance store's ephemeral nature.
questions.why_c_wrong: Amazon S3 is durable object storage, accessed over the network, and not directly attached to an EC2 instance's hardware at all.
questions.why_d_wrong: Amazon EFS is a managed, durable, shared file system accessible from multiple instances over the network, with data persisting independently of any single instance's lifecycle.

questions.question_text: Which statement best describes the AWS Cloud benefit of agility?
questions.explanation_correct: Agility in the AWS Cloud refers to the speed at which teams can access compute resources. Instead of waiting weeks for hardware procurement, a developer can launch new resources in minutes, try an idea, and decommission it if it doesn't work — at low cost and low risk.
questions.option_a: The ability to provision new resources in minutes instead of weeks, allowing experimentation at low cost
questions.option_b: The practice of replicating data across multiple Availability Zones
questions.option_c: The use of consolidated billing across multiple AWS accounts
questions.option_d: The encryption of data at rest using AWS KMS
questions.why_b_wrong: Replicating data across Availability Zones is a resiliency and durability practice, not a definition of agility.
questions.why_c_wrong: Consolidated billing is a cost-management and account-governance feature within AWS Organizations, unrelated to the speed of provisioning resources.
questions.why_d_wrong: Encrypting data at rest with KMS is a security practice. It doesn't describe the speed or flexibility benefit that agility refers to.

questions.question_text: A gaming company has players across Asia, Europe, and North America. Players in Europe report higher latency than players in North America, where the company's only server is located. What is the most appropriate way to use AWS global infrastructure to solve this?
questions.explanation_correct: Deploying into an AWS Region that is geographically closer to a group of users reduces the physical distance data has to travel, which lowers latency. AWS's global footprint of Regions exists specifically so that workloads can be placed near end users.
questions.option_a: Increase the size of the existing EC2 instance in North America
questions.option_b: Deploy the application into an additional AWS Region closer to European players
questions.option_c: Enable versioning on the application's S3 bucket
questions.option_d: Move the application to a single larger Availability Zone
questions.why_a_wrong: A larger instance increases compute capacity in the same physical location; it does nothing to reduce the network distance between European users and a North American data center.
questions.why_c_wrong: S3 versioning is a data-protection feature for object storage. It has no effect on application latency for end users.
questions.why_d_wrong: An Availability Zone is a physical location within a single Region. Making it 'larger' is not a real AWS concept, and a single AZ in North America would still be far from European users.

questions.question_text: Which TWO actions should a company take immediately to protect its AWS account root user? (Select TWO)
questions.explanation_correct: Enabling MFA (A) adds a critical second authentication factor beyond the password, and deleting root access keys (B) removes a dangerous form of programmatic access that's rarely needed and frequently targeted by attackers. Together these are the two most important immediate steps to lock down the root user.
questions.option_a: Enable multi-factor authentication (MFA) on the root user
questions.option_b: Delete the root user's access keys if any exist
questions.option_c: Use the root user for daily administrative tasks so the security team can monitor it closely
questions.option_d: Share the root user password with all senior engineers for convenience
questions.option_e: Disable CloudTrail logging on the root account to reduce noise
questions.why_c_wrong: The root user should be used as rarely as possible, only for the handful of tasks that explicitly require it — not for routine administrative work.
questions.why_d_wrong: Sharing root credentials, even internally, is a serious security violation; credentials should never be shared between people.
questions.why_e_wrong: Disabling CloudTrail would remove visibility into account activity, which is the opposite of good security practice — it doesn't protect the root user at all.

questions.question_text: A developer wants to automate the creation of AWS resources as part of a script, rather than manually clicking through the AWS Management Console each time. Which option allows this?
questions.explanation_correct: The AWS CLI and AWS SDKs provide programmatic access to AWS services, allowing developers to script and automate resource creation, rather than relying solely on manual interaction through the web-based console.
questions.option_b: The AWS Command Line Interface (CLI) or an AWS SDK
questions.why_a_wrong: The Management Console is a graphical, manual interface — it isn't designed for scripting or automation.
questions.why_c_wrong: AWS Artifact is a compliance document repository; it has no role in provisioning resources programmatically.
questions.why_d_wrong: Amazon WorkSpaces provides virtual desktops for end users; it isn't a tool for automating resource provisioning.

questions.question_text: A company wants to evaluate whether its cloud architecture is using the most efficient compute, storage, and networking resources for its workload requirements, especially as demand changes over time. Which Well-Architected Framework pillar does this best align with?
questions.explanation_correct: Performance Efficiency is about using computing resources efficiently to meet system requirements and maintaining that efficiency as demand changes and technologies evolve — exactly the scenario described.
questions.why_b_wrong: Security focuses on protecting data, systems, and assets through risk assessments and mitigation strategies, not on matching resource types to performance needs.
questions.why_c_wrong: Cost Optimization focuses on avoiding unnecessary spend; while related, the question is specifically about whether resource types and configuration suit the workload, which is a performance question, not a cost question.
questions.why_d_wrong: Operational Excellence focuses on running and monitoring systems and improving processes and procedures, not on resource efficiency for performance.

questions.question_text: Which AWS resource helps customers identify whether their AWS environment follows best practices across cost optimization, performance, security, and fault tolerance, providing a checklist-style report?
questions.explanation_correct: AWS Trusted Advisor inspects your AWS environment and provides recommendations across multiple categories — cost optimization, performance, security, fault tolerance, and service limits — helping you follow AWS best practices.
questions.why_b_wrong: Amazon Detective helps investigate and analyze the root cause of security findings after they've been detected, rather than providing a general best-practices checklist.
questions.why_c_wrong: AWS Firewall Manager centrally manages firewall rules like WAF and Shield Advanced across an organization; it's a management tool, not a general best-practices advisor.
questions.why_d_wrong: Amazon Cognito manages authentication for customer-facing applications and has no role in best-practice recommendations.

questions.question_text: A manufacturing company wants to connect thousands of factory sensors to the cloud, allowing them to securely send telemetry data and receive commands. Which AWS service category and service supports this use case?
questions.explanation_correct: AWS IoT Core is a managed service that lets internet-connected devices, such as factory sensors, securely connect to and interact with AWS services, supporting both sending telemetry data and receiving commands at scale.
questions.option_a: AWS IoT Core, an Internet of Things service for connecting and managing devices
questions.option_b: Amazon Connect, a contact center service
questions.option_c: Amazon AppStream 2.0, a desktop application streaming service
questions.option_d: AWS CodePipeline, a continuous delivery service
questions.why_b_wrong: Amazon Connect is designed for customer service contact centers, completely unrelated to connecting physical IoT devices.
questions.why_c_wrong: Amazon AppStream 2.0 streams desktop applications to users' browsers; it has no role in device connectivity.
questions.why_d_wrong: AWS CodePipeline automates software release pipelines for application code; it isn't designed for connecting physical sensors or devices.

questions.question_text: A company wants to run short-lived code in response to events, such as resizing an image immediately after it's uploaded to S3, without provisioning or managing any servers. Which AWS service fits this use case?
questions.explanation_correct: AWS Lambda is a serverless compute service that runs code in response to events — such as an object being uploaded to S3 — without requiring you to provision or manage any servers. You pay only for the compute time consumed.
questions.why_a_wrong: Amazon EC2 requires you to provision and manage virtual servers yourself, which is more operational overhead than needed for short, event-driven tasks.
questions.why_c_wrong: AWS Outposts extends AWS infrastructure to on-premises locations; it's unrelated to short, event-driven serverless execution.
questions.why_d_wrong: Amazon Lightsail provides simplified virtual private servers for simple web applications, not an event-driven, serverless execution model.

questions.question_text: Which AWS Cloud Adoption Framework (AWS CAF) benefit is most associated with reducing the risk of outdated infrastructure and unpatched systems during a migration to AWS?
questions.explanation_correct: AWS CAF identifies reduced business risk as a core benefit of cloud adoption, including improved security posture, compliance, and resilience — for example, by moving away from aging on-premises hardware and unpatched legacy systems toward managed, continuously updated AWS services.
questions.why_a_wrong: Increased revenue is a possible outcome of faster innovation, but it isn't the benefit specifically tied to reducing infrastructure risk.
questions.why_c_wrong: Increased staff turnover is not a benefit AWS CAF describes — quite the opposite; CAF emphasizes building staff skills.
questions.why_d_wrong: Improved marketing reach is unrelated to AWS CAF's framework of business, people, governance, platform, security, and operations perspectives.

questions.question_text: A finance team wants to receive an automatic alert when AWS spending is forecasted to exceed a specific monthly amount. Which AWS service should they use?
questions.explanation_correct: AWS Budgets allows you to set custom cost or usage thresholds and receive alerts when actual or forecasted spending exceeds those thresholds, making it the right tool for proactive spend monitoring.
questions.why_b_wrong: The AWS Pricing Calculator estimates costs before deploying a workload; it doesn't monitor actual ongoing spend or send alerts.
questions.why_c_wrong: The AWS Cost and Usage Report provides the most comprehensive and granular raw billing data for detailed analysis, but it doesn't natively send threshold-based alerts the way Budgets does.
questions.why_d_wrong: AWS Marketplace is a catalog for purchasing third-party software; it has no budget alerting functionality.

questions.question_text: Which migration approach involves moving an application to AWS with minimal or no changes to the application's architecture, often used as a fast first step in a migration?
questions.explanation_correct: Rehosting, also known as 'lift-and-shift,' moves an application to the cloud with little to no modification. It's typically the fastest migration approach and is often used to get initial cloud benefits before optimizing further.
questions.why_a_wrong: Refactoring involves re-architecting an application to take full advantage of cloud-native features, which requires significant code changes — the opposite of a minimal-change approach.
questions.why_c_wrong: Repurchasing means replacing an existing application with a different product, often a SaaS solution, rather than moving the existing application as-is.
questions.why_d_wrong: Retiring means decommissioning an application that is no longer needed, not migrating it.

questions.question_text: Before deploying a new workload, a company wants to estimate the monthly cost of running a specific combination of EC2 instances, storage, and data transfer, without actually creating any resources. Which AWS tool is designed for this?
questions.explanation_correct: The AWS Pricing Calculator lets you build out a hypothetical architecture and estimate its monthly and upfront costs before deploying anything, which is exactly the planning use case described.
questions.why_b_wrong: Cost Explorer analyzes actual historical spend after resources have already been used; it doesn't estimate costs for resources that don't exist yet.
questions.why_c_wrong: AWS Budgets monitors and alerts on actual or forecasted spend against a threshold; it isn't designed for pre-deployment architecture cost estimation.
questions.why_d_wrong: The Cost and Usage Report provides detailed historical billing data for resources already in use, not a forward-looking estimate for a planned deployment.

questions.question_text: Which of the following best describes the concept of 'undifferentiated heavy lifting' that AWS aims to remove from customers' responsibilities?
questions.explanation_correct: Undifferentiated heavy lifting refers to the operational tasks — like hardware maintenance, power, cooling, and physical security — that every company must handle on-premises but that don't actually differentiate one business from another. AWS takes on this burden so customers can focus on what makes their business unique.
questions.option_a: Tasks like racking servers, managing power and cooling, and patching physical hardware that don't differentiate a business from its competitors
questions.option_b: Designing a company's unique business logic and customer-facing application features
questions.option_c: Choosing which AWS Region to deploy a workload in
questions.option_d: Writing custom application code for a company's core product
questions.why_b_wrong: Designing unique business logic is exactly the differentiated work that AWS frees companies up to focus on — it's the opposite of undifferentiated heavy lifting.
questions.why_c_wrong: Choosing a Region is a lightweight architectural decision, not heavy infrastructure work.
questions.why_d_wrong: Writing custom application code is differentiated, valuable work specific to a company's product, not generic infrastructure overhead.

questions.question_text: Under the AWS shared responsibility model, who is responsible for the global infrastructure, including Regions, Availability Zones, and edge locations?
questions.explanation_correct: AWS is solely responsible for the global infrastructure — the physical Regions, Availability Zones, and edge locations, including the hardware, software, networking, and facilities that run AWS services. This falls under 'security of the cloud.'
questions.option_d: Both AWS and the customer equally
questions.why_a_wrong: The customer has no role in maintaining the physical infrastructure; their responsibility starts at the level of the resources they configure.
questions.why_c_wrong: AWS Partners may help customers with their own configurations, but the underlying global infrastructure is managed exclusively by AWS itself.
questions.why_d_wrong: This is not a shared responsibility — global infrastructure sits entirely on AWS's side of the model.

questions.question_text: A company is migrating an on-premises Oracle database to Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL and needs to both convert the database schema and migrate the data with minimal downtime. Which combination of AWS services supports this migration?
questions.explanation_correct: When migrating between different database engines (a 'heterogeneous' migration, such as Oracle to PostgreSQL), AWS Schema Conversion Tool converts the source schema and code to be compatible with the target engine, while AWS Database Migration Service handles migrating the actual data, supporting minimal-downtime migrations.
questions.option_a: Amazon CloudFront and AWS Direct Connect
questions.option_b: AWS Schema Conversion Tool (SCT) for schema conversion and AWS Database Migration Service (DMS) for data migration
questions.option_d: AWS Budgets and AWS Cost Explorer
questions.why_a_wrong: CloudFront and Direct Connect are content delivery and networking services; neither converts schemas or migrates database data.
questions.why_c_wrong: Amazon Polly (text-to-speech) and Amazon Lex (conversational AI) are machine learning services completely unrelated to database migration.
questions.why_d_wrong: AWS Budgets and Cost Explorer are cost management tools; they play no role in performing a database migration.

questions.question_text: A company wants to design its workload to remain available even if an entire data center experiences a power outage. Which TWO approaches help achieve this using AWS global infrastructure? (Select TWO)
questions.explanation_correct: Availability Zones (AZs) are physically separate data centers within a Region, each with independent power, cooling, and networking. Spreading resources across multiple AZs (A) and load-balancing traffic between them (C) means that if one AZ loses power, the others continue serving traffic without interruption.
questions.option_a: Deploy resources across multiple Availability Zones within a Region
questions.option_b: Use a single large EC2 instance to simplify management
questions.option_c: Distribute the workload across at least two Availability Zones with a load balancer
questions.option_d: Store all application logs locally on the instance's root volume
questions.option_e: Disable automatic backups to reduce storage costs
questions.why_b_wrong: A single large instance is a single point of failure — if its host or AZ fails, the entire workload goes down regardless of instance size.
questions.why_d_wrong: Storing logs only on local/root storage means they're lost if the instance terminates, and this has no bearing on availability across data center failures.
questions.why_e_wrong: Disabling backups reduces cost but increases risk of data loss; it does nothing to protect against an AZ-level outage.

questions.question_text: A startup wants to launch a new product feature quickly to test market demand before committing significant engineering resources. Which AWS Cloud characteristic most directly supports this approach?
questions.explanation_correct: Agility allows teams to provision resources quickly, experiment cheaply, and pivot fast if an idea doesn't work. This is the foundation of being able to test a feature with real users before investing heavily in it.
questions.why_a_wrong: Sustainability concerns minimizing environmental impact, not speed of experimentation.
questions.why_c_wrong: Compliance relates to meeting regulatory and industry standards, not to product experimentation speed.
questions.why_d_wrong: Data residency concerns where data is physically stored to meet legal requirements, unrelated to launching a feature quickly.

final_validation.topic_overlap_check: All 65 question stems are independently authored; no rotated/duplicate scenarios.
final_validation.schema_note: why_X_wrong fields are only generated for incorrect options; the correct answer's letter has no why_wrong field.
